p: separated himself: He who loves wisdom will separate himself from all impediments, and give himself wholly to seek it.
reveal itself: That is, that he may talk licentiously of whatever comes to mind.
contempt: Meaning, such a one as condemns all others.
waters: Which can never be drawn empty, but always bring profit.
accept the person of the wicked: That is, to favour him and support him.
innermost parts of the belly: They are soon believed and enter most deeply.
into it: He shows the refuge of the godly against all trouble.
a wounded spirit who can bear: The mind can well bear the infirmity of the body, but when the spirit is wounded, it is hard to sustain.
maketh room for him: Gets him liberty to speak, and the favour of them that are esteemed.
He that is first in his: He who speaks first, is best heard from the wicked judge, but when his adversary enquires out the matter it turns to his shame.
causeth contentions to cease: If a controversy cannot otherwise be decided, it is best to cast lots to know whose the thing will be.
parteth between the mighty: Appeases their controversy, who are so stout that they cannot otherwise be pacified.
bars of a castle: Which for the strength of it will not bow or yield.
love it shall eat the fruit: By the using the tongue well or evil, comes the fruit of it either good or bad.
wife findeth a good thing: He who is joined with a virtuous woman in marriage is blessed by the Lord, as in Pr 19:14.
than a brother: That is, often such are found who are more ready to do pleasure, than he that is more bound by duty.
